questions.question: If MADRAS can be written as ARSARS, how can ARKONAM be written in that code?
questions.questionHtml: If MADRAS can be written as ARSARS, how can ARKONAM be written in that code?
questions.solution:
Logic:

MADRAS → write twice → MADRASMADRAS
Pick even positions → A, R, S, A, R, S
So code = ARSARS ✅

ARKONAM → write twice →ARKONAMARKONAM

Even positions = R, O, A, A, K, N, M

Code = ROAAKNM

questions.question: Which term of the series 5, 8, 11, 14, …….... is 320?
questions.questionHtml: Which term of the series 5, 8, 11, 14, …….... is 320?
questions.solution:
Solution:

The series is: 5, 8, 11, 14, …
This is an Arithmetic Progression (AP).

General term of an AP:
Tn = a + (n – 1) × d

Here, Tn = 320
→ 320 = 5 + (n – 1) × 3
→ 320 – 5 = (n – 1) × 3
→ 315 = (n – 1) × 3
→ n – 1 = 105
→ n = 106

Solution:

Check the terms:

So, the rule is: nth term = 3 × n²

Next term = 3 × 7² = 3 × 49 = 147

Other logic: You can try double difference to find the answer.

questions.question: If the first three letters of the word COMPREHENSION are reversed, then the last three letters are added and then the remaining letters are reversed and added, then which letter will be exactly in the middle?
questions.questionHtml: If the first three letters of the word COMPREHENSION are reversed, then the last three letters are added and then the remaining letters are reversed and added, then which letter will be exactly in the middle?
questions.solution:
Solution:
Word = COMPREHENSION
Step 1: Reverse first 3 letters → MOC
Step 2: Last 3 letters → ION
Step 3: Remaining letters → PREHENS (reverse it → SNEHERP)

Now arrange: MOC + ION + SNEHERP = MOCIONSNEHERP

Middle letter = 7th letter = S

questions.question: If A + B > C + D and B + C > A + D, then it is definite that
questions.questionHtml: If A + B > C + D and B + C > A + D, then it is definite that
questions.solution:
Solution:
Given:
A + B > C + D …(i)
B + C > A + D …(ii)

Adding (i) and (ii), we get:

(A + B) + (B + C) > (C + D) + (A + D)

⇒ A + 2B + C > C + 2D + A

⇒ 2B > 2D

⇒ B > D
